who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), executor, host round 2 piece front, third pass (late reads in a surface's shape)
where: crates/blaze-keyed/src/record.rs `late_id(which, name)` (no unit); crates/blaze-host/src/host.rs:85 `Request::late` and :441 `Universe { outside: self.request.late }` (one table for every unit); crates/blaze-unitkey/src/unit.rs `LateAnswer { file, late, name }` (per file, by the literal the call wrote)
what: A late read is unit-relative (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` is each crate's own) and an include's literal is file-relative (two files' `include_str!("a.txt")` read different files), but its fact id names neither, and the host answers every unit from one table. A surface or body that asks a late read gets another unit's value, or a request with two such values cannot be answered.
cost: an hour finding which side defines what a late read's name and answer are; blaze-front had to pick (a variable's name; an include's path in its source root; the host's var_answer and file_answer) and say so
cause: the late-read id was designed from blaze-unitkey's per-file key rows, before any task asked one through Universe::answer
class: an id that leaves out a coordinate its value depends on (rule keys-cover-every-input)
prevention: the outside table a task's universe holds is its unit's (per asker), and an include is named by its resolved path, not its literal; a test asks one variable from two units with two values
workaround: blaze-front checks every late answer against the value its expansions saw and fails LATE_MOVED where they differ, so a wrong table fails loudly, never files
fix: blaze-host: a late table per unit in `Request`; blaze-unitkey: name an include by its resolved source-root path
